macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Stocks rise ahead of Fed decision and major technology earnings
items.summary: U.S. equities gained in the latest session, with the Nasdaq Composite up 0.8%, the S&P 500 up 0.7%, and the Dow up 0.3%. Futures were little changed to modestly higher Tuesday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s policy decision and earnings from major technology companies.

items.title: Fed, ECB and BOJ decisions dominate markets
items.summary: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to hold interest rates steady Wednesday after a 25-basis-point increase in September, while the European Central Bank and Bank of Japan are also expected to leave policy unchanged this week. Markets are nevertheless pricing in potential further Fed tightening as inflation remains elevated.

items.title: Technology shares lead global market gains
items.summary: A rally in technology stocks lifted global equities ahead of results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon. The Stoxx Europe 600 and MSCI World Index were both higher, while Asian markets also gained amid enthusiasm surrounding artificial-intelligence companies.

items.title: Anthropic IPO filing boosts artificial-intelligence sentiment
items.summary: Anthropic filed for an initial public offering, intensifying investor interest in the AI sector despite the company reporting significant losses and security-related concerns. The filing helped support technology shares ahead of major AI-related earnings and announcements.

items.title: Major companies report mixed quarterly results
items.summary: Coca-Cola raised its full-year outlook on strong international demand, PayPal increased its earnings guidance despite missing revenue estimates, and UPS lifted its annual guidance. Whirlpool reported a quarterly loss and revenue miss, while Boeing signaled caution about increasing 737 Max production.

items.title: HSBC reports sharp profit growth and announces buyback
items.summary: HSBC reported third-quarter pretax profit of $9.63 billion, up 32% from a year earlier, maintained its dividend and announced a new share-buyback program.

items.title: Broadcom arranges $63 billion financing for Anthropic-related AI capacity
items.summary: Broadcom announced a $63 billion financing structure involving Bank of America, Citigroup, Blackstone and Morgan Stanley to support the deployment of AI computing capacity for Anthropic.

items.title: Meta expands equity fundraising for AI investment
items.summary: Meta Platforms increased its planned equity fundraising to $97.5 billion to finance artificial-intelligence expansion. Meta and Nvidia also announced plans to expand their collaboration on AI models.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Ripple receives final U.S. approval for national trust bank
items.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency approved Ripple National Trust Bank, which is intended to manage reserves for Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin and provide institutional crypto custody. The bank will not take deposits or make loans.

items.title: Bitcoin hovers near $80,000 as derivatives leverage rises
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $79,700–$80,200, while Bitcoin derivatives open interest reached approximately $28.18 billion ahead of a Federal Reserve decision. About $140.8 million in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, with long positions accounting for 56.9% of losses.

items.title: South Korea considers delaying crypto-gains tax until 2029
items.summary: South Korea’s government is reportedly considering a fourth postponement of its planned 22% tax on cryptocurrency gains, which is currently scheduled to begin in January 2027.

items.title: Canada opens consultation on stablecoin regulations
items.summary: Canada published draft stablecoin rules that would require non-bank issuers to register with the Bank of Canada, maintain full reserves at Canadian institutions, provide redemption within three business days, and prohibit yield payments to holders.

items.title: Kraken launches CFTC-regulated perpetual futures for U.S. users
items.summary: Kraken introduced perpetual futures markets for U.S. customers through an integration with Hyperliquid, marking a notable expansion of regulated crypto derivatives access.

items.title: GameStop transfers its Bitcoin holdings to Coinbase Prime
items.summary: GameStop reportedly moved all 4,710 BTC in its disclosed Bitcoin treasury, valued at roughly $422 million at the cited market price, to Coinbase Prime. The transfer prompted speculation about whether the company may sell or reorganize its holdings.

items.title: Solana Foundation launches institutional settlement standard
items.summary: The Solana Foundation launched Solana DvP, an open-source delivery-versus-payment standard designed for atomic settlement of tokenized assets and developed with input from J.P. Morgan.

items.title: Initia pauses blockchain after token-minting exploit
items.summary: Initia reportedly halted its blockchain after a bug allowed an attacker to mint and move approximately $2.7 million worth of tokens.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI announces three purported AI research breakthroughs
items.summary: OpenAI says its models generated new results in mathematics, theoretical physics and computer science, including claims involving the Kakeya/local smoothing conjecture, Yang–Mills theory and the Exponential Time Hypothesis. Experts are being asked to scrutinize the work, and the claims have not yet been independently validated.

items.title: Anthropic files for a Nasdaq IPO
items.summary: Anthropic has reportedly filed to go public under the ticker ANT. The filing highlights rapid revenue growth, substantial losses, enterprise adoption and governance provisions intended to preserve the company’s safety mission.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly launched GPT-6.1 Terra, a lower-cost model aimed at everyday agentic work, coding, writing and screenshot understanding. Reports describe faster performance and reduced API pricing compared with higher-tier models.

items.title: Microsoft releases Decision-1 for calibrated classification
items.summary: Microsoft introduced Decision-1, a 9-billion-parameter model designed to evaluate supplied content against predefined answer choices and produce calibrated probabilities. Its intended uses include routing, prioritization, verification and workflow control rather than general conversation.

items.title: Hugging Face publishes Carbon-X DNA language model
items.summary: Hugging Face reportedly released Carbon-X under the Apache 2.0 license, enabling analysis of raw DNA sequences and English-language responses. Reported benchmark results place it close to leading proprietary systems on the cited evaluation.

items.title: NVIDIA and Meta expand AI-agent collaboration
items.summary: NVIDIA and Meta are reportedly expanding cooperation around the Muse model partnership and agent infrastructure, including NVIDIA’s OpenShell reference architecture and Sentry monitoring tools. NVIDIA also plans a multibillion-dollar investment tied to Meta’s equity offering.

items.title: Ant Group launches Lingguang 2.0 assistant
items.summary: Ant Group reportedly released Lingguang 2.0, an assistant designed to proactively identify tasks, monitor progress and send reminders after receiving user authorization. The launch reflects a broader shift toward persistent, task-oriented AI agents.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: U.S. video game spending fell 1% in September
items.summary: Circana reported that U.S. spending on video game content, hardware and accessories declined 1% year over year to $4.8 billion in September. Marvel’s Wolverine led monthly full-game sales, while NBA 2K27 became 2026’s best-selling game year to date.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero set for October 29 release
items.summary: S-Game’s action role-playing game Phantom Blade Zero is scheduled to launch on PC and PlayStation 5 on October 29, making it one of the week’s most notable releases.

items.title: EA reportedly plans major BioWare changes
items.summary: Electronic Arts reportedly plans to cut about 400 jobs, shut down BioWare and cancel projects including the studio’s next Mass Effect game, according to reporting cited in the industry roundup.

items.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exits to thousands of staff
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly offered voluntary departure packages to as many as 60,000 employees, a development with potential implications for its gaming organization and broader technology operations.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced adds New Game+
items.summary: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced received a New Game+ feature, expanding its replay options in a newly reported update.

items.title: Indie Treasures Sale brings together more than 200 studios
items.summary: More than 200 independent studios are participating in a Steam sale led by Toukana Interactive, intended to increase visibility for indie games ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI’s release.

items.title: Replaced wins Best Game at Central & Eastern European Game Awards
items.summary: Sad Cat Studios’ Replaced won Best Game at the Central & Eastern European Game Awards and collected three trophies overall after receiving six nominations.

items.title: Minecraft reportedly launches natively on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Minecraft was reported to be arriving as a native Nintendo Switch 2 release on October 27, with Vibrant Visuals and a Super Mario-themed pack; existing digital owners were reportedly eligible for a limited-time upgrade.

items.title: Carry1st expands esports and gaming commerce strategy
items.summary: Carry1st is refocusing on commerce through Carry1st Shop, Pay1st and Flow1st while continuing esports initiatives, including qualification pathways involving the Call of Duty: Mobile World Championship and Esports World Cup.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple unveils new iPad mini with OLED display
items.summary: Apple reportedly launched a redesigned iPad mini featuring an OLED display and a faster A20 Pro chip, marking a significant update to its smallest tablet line.

items.title: Apple launches 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip
items.summary: Apple reportedly introduced a 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by its next-generation M6 processor, with claimed battery life of up to 24 hours.

items.title: Apple adds M6 chip to iMac and entry-level MacBook Pro
items.summary: Apple reportedly expanded its M6 hardware lineup to include a new iMac and an entry-level MacBook Pro, making the processor available across more consumer devices.

items.title: Intel to acquire quantum software company Classiq
items.summary: Intel reportedly agreed to buy quantum-computing software firm Classiq for approximately $2.3 billion, signaling increased investment in quantum technology beyond conventional computing.

items.title: Tesla partners with Turo to promote Full Self-Driving
items.summary: Tesla is reportedly turning to car-sharing platform Turo to increase consumer exposure to its supervised Full Self-Driving system.

items.title: Autonomous excavator startup raises $600 million
items.summary: Bedrock Robotics, which develops autonomous-driving technology for excavators, reportedly raised $600 million in Series C funding at a valuation of about $4.1 billion.
